title: Session-aware marginal cost slice UX and export workflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Teams want to understand per-session economics for chat and conversational products: not just total token spend, but the marginal cost contributed by specific interactions, reruns, and system messages across a user session. Existing token-level panels at Redwood show per-route and per-token aggregates, but customers repeatedly ask for a session-first view that can attribute cost to the session timeline, easily export role-aware breakdowns for finance, and surface where caching/batching would have reduced spend.

Goal:
Design a Console panel that: (1) groups invocations into sessions and visualizes marginal cost slices over the session timeline, (2) breaks down cost by role (user, system, assistant, tools), model/version, and batching impact, (3) includes a CSV export template that finance/platform teams can ingest (session_id, user_id, start_ts, end_ts, per-invocation-token-counts, marginal-cost, amortized-system-cost, model_version, route, tags), and (4) surfaces quick suggestions for pricing-patterns (reserved vs per-usage) and estimated savings from applying caching/quantization.

Scope and constraints:
- Work as a design-first prototype for Console (no infra changes required for visualization).
- Backend will provide sessionized payloads via ENG-12744; prototype must tolerate partial fields (missing user_id, approximate timestamps).
- Exports must allow role-aware filtering and redaction for PII-sensitive fields (user_id optional).
- UX should scale from single-session drilldown to cohort-level comparisons (up to 10k sessions sampled).

Deliverables:
1) Figma prototype for "Session marginal cost" panel (list + timeline + slice inspector + export modal).
2) Export CSV schema and downloadable sample.
3) Interaction spec for how rollouts and canary views display cost regressions tied to model versions.
4) Hand-off package for ENG and PM including edge cases and accessibility notes.
design_decisions: Session-first list view: primary table surfaces session_id, user_display (optional), start/end, total_tokens, marginal_cost, primary_model
Timeline multi-track: each track represents role streams (user/system/assistant/tool) with colored stacked bars for token counts and a separate line overlay for marginal cost in USD
Slice inspector: click a timeline slice to open lateral panel that shows per-invocation tokens, KV-cache hits (if available), estimated batch savings, and 'why this cost changed' heuristics
Export schema includes an 'amortized_system_cost' column calculated by dividing shared system-token cost across session invocations; default export redacts user_id unless export role has permission
Quick-savings banner: when the UI detects repeated identical prefixes or long assistant responses, show a non-blocking suggestion linking to Optimize recommendations
Sampling for cohort views: UI will show 'sampled view' badge when session count exceeds 5k and include a link to full raw export via backend job
acceptance_criteria: Prototype Figma demonstrates list -> timeline -> slice inspector flow with realistic synthetic data
Export modal allows toggling columns (include user_id, include raw prompts, include model_version) and produces CSV sample matching schema
Design spec documents failure states for missing timestamps, redaction warnings, and slow exports
PM review sign-off on pricing-pattern suggestions text and placement
Accessibility: timeline uses color + patterns and passes AA contrast; keyboard access to slice inspector works
open_questions: Backend: can ENG-12744 provide per-invocation 'kv_cache_hit' boolean? If not, we need to mark estimated vs observed savings
Pricing: should quick-savings banner include estimated $savings for reserved capacity or just percent token reduction? Need PM guidance
Export retention: how long should generated export files persist? Ops input needed for S3 lifecycle
Sampling: define tradeoffs for cohort sampling—should we sample by session start-time distribution or user?
